newsitem.title: USA: Consumer protections added to U.S. bank reform.
newsitem.headline: Consumer protections added to U.S. bank reform.

text.p: The House Banking Committee on Thursday approved an amendment to bank reform legislation spelling out a series of measures to protect consumers.
If the bill becomes law, banks, insurances companies and securities firms would be able to combine and offer consumers one-stop shopping for financial services.

Under the amendment, sponsored by New York Democrat John LaFalce, companies would have make clear disclosure about the risks of various products. Companies also could not coerce consumers into into buying products as a condition of receiving a loan or other service.
Consumer groups complained that under the original proposal, large financial companies offering a diverse array of products might mislead or overcharge consumers.
